item.title: Farmers-herders clashes reduced in Kano — Commissioner
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Kano State Government says clashes between farmers and herders have reduced significantly following the demarcation of 1,270 kilometres of cattle routes across the state. The Commissioner for Agriculture and Natural Resources, Dr Danjuma Mahmoud, disclosed this on Tuesday while outlining the achievements of the ministry. He said the demarcation had helped address recurring disputes between farmers and herders by providing designated routes for the movement of livestock. According to him, the initiative formed part of the state government’s efforts to tackle longstanding challenges in the agricultural sector and promote peaceful coexistence between farming and pastoral communities. “One important problem that I want to reiterate is the intractable problem of clashes between farmers and herders. We have made significant progress in that regard. “Our project provided demarcated cattle routes covering about 1,270 kilometres across the state. That is why you now hear that clashes between herders and farmers have reduced to the barest minimum in Kano State,” he said. Mahmoud said the ministry had also implemented interventions to boost agricultural production, including the rehabilitation of irrigation facilities and the expansion of cultivable farmland. He disclosed that more than 1,200 acres of farmland had been recovered through the clearing of irrigation channels and rehabilitation of canals at major irrigation sites. The commissioner added that the state government, in collaboration with the African Development Bank-supported Agricultural Transformation Agenda Support Programme (ATASP), had recovered more than 200 additional acres for irrigation. He said the government had secured approval to develop 11 mini dams and irrigation facilities across 11 local government areas. “When completed, these projects will provide about 2,000 additional acres of irrigable farmland in the state,” he said. Mahmoud further disclosed that the ministry had completed more than 70 milk collection centres to improve milk handling and storage in pastoral communities. He said the centres were equipped with storage facilities and solar-powered cooling systems to preserve milk before transportation to markets. item.description: … As Camp faces setback amid rift By Henry Umoru ABUJA- AS Campaigns have begun ahead of 2027 general elections, the Obi-Kwankwaso (OK) Movement has warned the Nigeria Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council and the Obidient Movement not to cause friction in the camp of the NDC Presidential candidate, Peter Obi. Recall that crisis had last month reared its head between the leadership of the party and the support group when the OK Movement unveiled its presidential campaign council and the leadership of the party immediately took a swipe at the development as it rejected the composition of the Campaign Council. The NDC maintained that the role of support groups should be limited to supporting the party and its candidates, rather than assuming the functions of a political party. The OK Movement on its part, resisted the NDC’s position, saying it had a mandate to ensure that Obi and Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso were elected in 2027. This led to strained relations between the two groups. Reacting to the development, the United Kingdom Coordinator of the OK Movement, Adebayo Brown, on Tuesday accused leaders of the NDC PCC and the Obidient Movement of encouraging divisions among groups associated with Peter Obi’s 2027 presidential ambition. item.title: Defence Minister welcomes reinstated permanent secretary
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (Rtd), on Tuesday welcomed the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry, Mr Richard Pheelangwah, back to office following the lifting of his suspension and his reinstatement by the Federal Government. Musa expressed confidence in maintaining a cordial working relationship with the permanent secretary, stressing the need to build on their existing synergy to advance the ministry’s mandate. Pheelangwah, in his remarks, expressed appreciation for the opportunity to resume duty and pledged to discharge his responsibilities with renewed dedication, professionalism and commitment to national service. A statement by the minister’s Special Adviser on Media, Leah Katung-Babatunde, said the meeting reaffirmed the ministry’s commitment to institutional continuity, effective service delivery and the pursuit of Nigeria’s defence and security objectives. item.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri The Borno State Police Command has arrested 103 suspected criminals in connection to combat substance abuse, violence, thuggery and other social vices. The arrests were carried out in Maiduguri metropolis between the months of October 29 to November 2nd, 2026, with support from its Rapid Response Squad (RRS) – Social Vices Unit. This was disclosed by the Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Keneth Daso in a statement he signed on Tuesday. The statement reads partly: “In a sustained effort to rid Maiduguri metropolis of criminal elements and combat substance abuse, violence, thuggery and other social vices, the Borno State Police Command, through its Rapid Response Squad (RRS) – Social Vices Unit, has recorded a major operational breakthrough with the arrest of 103 suspects during a week-long township patrol and coordinated raid operations conducted between 29th October and 2nd November 2026. “The operations, carried out on the directives of the Commissioner of Police, CP Naziru Abdulmajid, psc, involved a combined team of Police operatives and other relevant security agencies. “The joint operations focused on identified crime-prone areas and security hotspots across the metropolis, including Gwange, Santiago, Texaco, Ajari, Gadan Zare, Budum, Shehuri, Bulabulin, Abbaganaram, Baga Road, Gidan Dambe, UNIMAID 202 Housing Estate, Mairi Kuwait, Bakari, Zanneri, Polo, Giwa Barrack Area, Kwanan Yobe, Jiddari, Kaleri, Damboa Road, Circular and Moduganari, among other locations. “The operations resulted in the arrest of 103 suspects for offences bordering on public nuisance, possession and sale of illicit drugs, and possession of dangerous weapons. “The suspects are undergoing preliminary screening and investigation, while those found culpable will be prosecuted in accordance with the law”. item.title: Atiku accuses DSS of plotting to disrupt ADC rally in Sokoto
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — Former Vice President and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Atiku Abubakar, has accused the leadership of the Department of State Services, DSS, of recruiting protesters to create disorder in Sokoto and provide a pretext for imposing a curfew to stop the party’s campaign rally. Atiku said the alleged plot was part of a broader attempt by the President Bola Tinubu-led administration to frustrate opposition parties, undermine political competition and deny Nigerians the freedom to choose their leaders ahead of the 2027 general election. Briefing journalists in Abuja on Tuesday, the former vice president alleged that public facilities meant for campaign activities had been blocked and logistical support withheld in Sokoto, describing the developments as deliberate efforts to deny the ADC a level playing field. He said information available to the party indicated that protesters were being mobilised from an office behind Zenith Bank on Koko Road, with trucks deployed to strategic locations, including a roundabout. According to him, the protesters were causing gridlock, threatening commuters and beating some residents, while some had moved away from the roundabout to find shade. “This is not intelligence work. It is political interference dressed in official uniform,” Atiku said. “Security agencies exist to protect Nigerians and uphold the law, not to recruit protesters or help a political party manufacture a crisis.” He called on security officers allegedly involved in the mobilisation to stop immediately and return to their constitutional duty of impartial service. Atiku accused the Tinubu administration of devoting much of its energy over the past three and a half years to weakening credible opposition, alleging that its strategy of absorbing former opposition figures into the APC was aimed at reducing Nigeria to a one-party state in all but name. The former vice president also linked the alleged obstruction of the rally to the economic hardship facing Nigerians, saying the government should be defending its record on the rising cost of food, transport, fuel, electricity and other essentials rather than trying to stop opposition campaigns. “Families are struggling to feed their children, pay school fees and keep their businesses alive,” he said. “That is the record this government should be defending before the people, instead of trying to stop a rally.” Atiku pledged that an ADC government would make life affordable through policies to support local production, strengthen food production, create jobs and reduce the cost of doing business. He said the party would also pursue a targeted production subsidy tied to fuel refined in Nigeria, aimed at providing measurable relief to consumers while strengthening domestic industry. item.title: 2027: DLA suspends Adebisi’s presidential campaign, refers him to EFCC, police
item.description: …distances itself from candidate, warns members against promoting his candidature By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The Democratic Leadership Alliance (DLA) has suspended all presidential campaign activities by its 2027 candidate, Moses Adebisi, pending the outcome of disciplinary proceedings against him and ongoing criminal investigations by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) and the police. The party said it had withdrawn institutional backing from Adebisi’s campaign over concerns arising from a personal financial undertaking allegedly made before his emergence as its presidential candidate, including a dud cheque, while reserving the right to take further political decisions on its participation in the presidential election. The position was contained in a statement by the party’s National Chairman and Leader, Barr. Samuel Memeh, who said the DLA had initiated disciplinary proceedings against Adebisi and referred the matter to the EFCC and the Inspector-General of Police for independent investigation. According to the statement, the party’s National Disciplinary Committee invited Adebisi to appear before it on August 30, 2026, following a letter dated August 29. “Following that proceeding, the Committee issued a directive suspending all presidential campaign activities and public appearances relating to his candidature pending further resolution,” Memeh said. The party said it would not assume responsibility for personal financial undertakings or transactions entered into by any individual without its authorisation, stressing that Adebisi remained personally responsible for his commitments. It also distanced itself from his personal activities and political engagements that were not expressly authorised by the party, warning the public against treating his representations as official DLA commitments. The party reaffirmed that all presidential campaign activities and public projection relating to Adebisi’s candidature remained suspended until further notice. It said further decisions would be taken after the disciplinary committee submitted its recommendations, adding that it reserved the right to determine its political participation in the 2027 presidential election. The DLA also directed its candidates and campaign organisations to stop promoting Adebisi as its presidential candidate while the suspension remained in force. “All campaigns and public political activities undertaken by our candidates shall be regulated, coordinated, and supervised by the National Campaign Council, under the authority of the National Working Committee and the National Leadership,” Memeh said. The party warned that candidates who displayed Adebisi’s photographs in campaign posters, flyers, banners, billboards or digital materials in ways suggesting official endorsement could face disciplinary action. It, however, urged Nigerians to support its candidates contesting governorship, National Assembly, state Houses of Assembly and other elective positions

item.title: EFCC Uncovers Chinese-Operated Illegal Oil Refinery In Ogun
item.description: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) says it has uncovered an illegal oil refinery allegedly operated by Chinese nationals in the Ogere area of Ogun State. The Commission disclosed that the operation, carried out on Saturday, October 31, 2026, by operatives of its Lagos Zonal Directorate 2, followed intelligence gathering and surveillance on the activities of illegal sludge oil refiners. The development was contained in a statement issued on Tuesday by the EFCC Head of Media and Publicity, Dele Oyewale. The illegal oil refinery allegedly operated by Chinese nationals. X/@officialEFCC According to the Commission, the refinery was deserted when operatives stormed the premises, following an earlier crackdown on four illegal lithium processing plants in the area. However, they discovered waste products from the refining process, as well as underground tanks believed to have been used for heating and processing sludge oil. “Two of the underground tanks inspected contained substances suspected to be Automotive Gas Oil (AGO), otherwise known as diesel,” the statement said. The EFCC said preliminary investigations showed that the operators sourced sludge oil, also known as black sludge, from Warri in Delta State and Port Harcourt in Rivers State before transporting it to the facility in Ogere for processing. The illegal oil refinery allegedly operated by Chinese nationals. X/@officialEFCC It explained that further investigations indicated that the operators subjected the sludge oil to intense heat, allowing lighter petroleum components to pass through a series of chambers and filters in a process believed to produce Automotive Gas Oil (AGO) for sale in the Nigerian market. The Commission added that security personnel at the facility told its operatives that the Chinese operators never disclosed their identities or the name of the company behind the operation. Operatives of the Lagos Zonal Directorate 2 have since taken over the premises as investigations continue to establish the identities of the operators, ownership of the facility and the full extent of the suspected illegal activities and economic sabotage. item.title: Fresh oil spill disrupts fishing in Bayelsa community
item.description: By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa A fresh crude oil spill has polluted the shoreline of Egweama community on Cape Formosa Island in Brass Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, disrupting fishing activities and leaving residents stranded. The incident, which occurred on Sunday, November 1, 2026, was documented in a field report by the Environmental Conservation Agriculture and Rural Development (ECARD). The organisation said the spill was reported to it the following day, with its Chief Operating Officer, Alagoa Morris, subsequently conducting a follow-up assessment. According to the report, crude oil had spread across the water surface along the Atlantic coastline, affecting the livelihood of residents who depend mainly on fishing. It said jerrycans, drums and plastic basins were seen filled with crude oil, while some youths were observed scooping the pollutant into containers on Monday morning. A resident, Ms Ebimiete David, said community members had spent several hours collecting crude oil from the shoreline. She said children first reported seeing crude oil along the shoreline between 5pm and 6pm on Sunday, adding that the volume increased when the tide came in around 8pm. David said residents continued scooping the oil into containers until about 3am, when the water receded and carried away a large quantity of the pollutant. Also recounting the impact of the spill, Chief Souyo Amasara-Inengite, described as the first settler at one of the fishing camps along the affected shoreline, said the incident had prevented fishermen from going to sea. He said the oil covered the water surface when they attempted to go fishing between 7pm and 8pm on Sunday, adding that some fishing nets had also been contaminated and damaged. “We are all stranded on land now. Just now I went out to the sea to drop my fishing nets but there was no way; everywhere is crude oil and I returned disappointed,” he said. Confirming the incident, Chairman of the Community Development Committee (CDC), Mr Tonye Yemoleigha, called for urgent intervention and cleanup. In a statement titled, “Oil spill: Egweama community cries out for immediate help, Cleanup,” Yemoleigha said the community was uncertain about the source of the spill. He, however, said unconfirmed reports from community sources suggested that it might have originated from the activities of Aiteo Oil Company, whose vessels transport crude from Nembe Creek to the Atlantic. Yemoleigha urged the Bayelsa State Government to intervene and ensure that the responsible oil company undertook immediate remedial action and cleanup. He also called for medical and relief materials to cushion the socioeconomic impact of the incident on affected residents. ECARD described the incident as another example of the recurring problem of “mystery spills”, in which the source of oil pollution remains unidentified and operating companies deny responsibility. item.title: Kebbi set to implement ₦70,000 transportation allowance for workers
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — The Kebbi State Government has said it is ready to implement a ₦70,000 transport allowance for workers in the state to cushion the high transport fares occasioned by the removal of fuel subsidy. The State Governor, Comrade Nasir Idris, disclosed this on Tuesday during an interview with journalists in Abuja. Recall that the Kebbi State Government approved a ₦75,000 minimum wage for state workers and an additional ₦17,650 for teachers. Asked whether the state would pay workers the ₦70,000 recently approved for federal workers, to be implemented from November, Governor Idris said he had already set up a committee for the implementation of the transport allowance. He expressed concern over the declining purchasing power of the current minimum wage due to economic hardship, adding that a committee under the Head of Service was currently working on a further adjustment. “I just came back from a journey, and, by God’s grace, I know what the Federal Government has decided to do for workers. You should also know that, being a labour leader, something must definitely be done for Kebbi State workers. “I have already set up a committee under the Head of Service, and they are working. I have said, time without number, that if the Federal Government increases workers’ salaries, Kebbi State will be among the first states to implement it. “The President has done well by approving the ₦70,000 transport intervention. The President believes that the purchasing power of the existing ₦70,000 national minimum wage has been affected by the economic situation. That is why he graciously approved the ₦70,000 transport allowance before the new minimum wage will be negotiated.” The Governor emphasised his commitment to maintaining industrial harmony by prioritising the needs of workers and artisans. To ensure conducive working conditions, the Comrade Governor said his administration had embarked on the development of workers’ housing projects, including a project for 155 houses and another for 250 units, some of which are expected to be commissioned by December. He also absorbed over 1,700 casual workers he inherited into full-time employment to ensure job security, while an additional 2,000 teachers and various health workers, including doctors, nurses, and pharmacists, have been recruited under his leadership. Governor Idris highlighted his efforts to foster better synergy and cooperation between workers and the government. On revenue generation and fiscal management, the former labour leader said significant improvements had been made in internally generated revenue by closing leakages. He asserted that revenue collection had increased significantly compared with previous administrations. The Governor said his administration does not owe workers’ salaries, pensions, gratuities, or other benefits, attributing the successful financial management to the prudent use of resources despite increased responsibilities. item.title: Tinubu’s Rivers rally to spotlight appointments, projects
item.description: By Daniel Abia PORT HARCOURT — Federal appointments secured by Rivers indigenes and infrastructure projects executed by the Federal Government are expected to feature prominently at the campaign rally for President Bola Tinubu in Port Harcourt on Saturday, November 7. The rally, scheduled to hold at the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium, is expected to attract political leaders, All Progressives Congress (APC) members and supporters from across Rivers State. A chieftain of the APC in the state, Barrister Princewill Dike, said the event would provide an opportunity to highlight the appointments and development projects credited to the Tinubu administration in Rivers. Dike, a member of the Publicity and Media Committee of the Tinubu Campaign Organisation in the state, listed several federal appointments secured by Rivers indigenes. They include Ambassador Desmond Akawor, Federal Commissioner representing Rivers State on the Revenue Mobilisation, Allocation and Fiscal Commission (RMAFC), whose appointment was approved by Tinubu in November 2023 and subsequently confirmed by the Senate. He also mentioned Boma Iyaye, Executive Director, Finance and Administration of the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC), and Chief Tony Okocha, who represents Rivers State on the commission’s governing board. Other appointees listed by Dike are Senator Magnus Abe, Chairman of the National Agency for the Great Green Wall, and Chief Victor Tombari Giadom, Chairman of the Nigerian Institute of Educational Planning and Administration. Dike also cited a disclosure reportedly made by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, on October 24, 2026, that Rivers State had secured at least 49 federal appointments under the Tinubu administration. The appointments, according to the reported disclosure, include directors-general, executive secretaries and heads of federal agencies. On infrastructure, Dike highlighted the 37.9-kilometre Bodo-Bonny Road, which was temporarily opened in December 2025, providing a direct road connection between Bonny Island and the mainland. He said the road had reduced the island’s long-standing dependence on river transportation and helicopter services. He also listed sections of the East-West Road, particularly the Eleme Junction-Port Harcourt-Ahoada and Eleme Junction-Onne Port corridors, among the Federal Government’s infrastructure interventions in the Niger Delta. Other projects cited include the 700-kilometre Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, which traverses nine states, including Rivers, Bayelsa, Akwa Ibom and Cross River. Dike further mentioned NDDC projects such as the Kaa-Ataba Bridge, linking Khana and Andoni Local Government Areas, and the Bonny Ring Road and Bridges being undertaken in collaboration with the Nigeria LNG Limited (NLNG). item.title: Senate steps down Barau’s Agricultural Revolution Bill
item.description: ….Ningi, Yahaya Abdullahi fault drafting, omnibus nature, non-circulation By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate on Tuesday stepped down the proposed Agricultural Revolution Bill, 2026, following a heated debate over its drafting, scope and failure to circulate printed copies to senators. The bill, sponsored by the Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Jibrin Barau (APC, Kano North), failed to scale second reading after several lawmakers raised concerns about its content and compliance with legislative procedures. Titled “A Bill for an Act to Provide a Comprehensive Legal Framework for Transformation and Modernisation of Agriculture in Nigeria, Promote Food Security, Agricultural Productivity, Mechanisation, Irrigation, Agricultural Financing, Agro-industrialisation, Rural Development and Climate-resilient Farming and for Related Matters,” the proposed legislation seeks to establish a framework for the transformation and sustainable development of the agricultural sector. Presenting its general principles on behalf of Barau, the Senate Whip, Senator Mohammed Tahir Monguno (APC, Borno North), said the legislation was necessary to address Nigeria’s food security challenges. Monguno said agriculture provided livelihoods for millions of Nigerians, accounting for about 70 per cent of employment and 40 per cent of the country’s Gross Domestic Product. He identified low productivity, inadequate mechanisation, limited irrigation infrastructure, high post-harvest losses, poor access to affordable financing, insecurity in farming communities and weak agricultural value chains as major challenges confronting the sector. According to him, the challenges had contributed to food insecurity, inflation and rising poverty, making it necessary to move beyond fragmented interventions towards a coordinated legal framework. He said the bill sought to reposition Nigerian agriculture from subsistence production to modern, technology-driven and commercially viable farming through mechanisation, improved seeds, agricultural research, extension services and irrigation development. It also proposed measures to strengthen the agricultural value chain through storage facilities, cold-chain infrastructure, agro-processing and improved market access. Seconding the bill, Senator Adamu Aliero (APC, Kebbi Central) said agriculture remained central to Nigeria’s economic diversification efforts and should be developed as a commercial venture rather than largely subsistence activity. He called for massive investment in mechanisation, research and development to improve agricultural productivity and increase farmers’ yields per hectare. Trouble, however, started when Senator Abdul Ningi (Bauchi Central) raised concerns about the bill’s drafting, although he described its objectives as timely and commendable. item.title: Ronaldo Jnr. earns first Portugal U17 call-up, could meet father at training ground
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Cristiano Ronaldo Jnr. has received his first call-up to Portugal’s Under-17 team, raising the possibility of meeting his father, Cristiano Ronaldo, at the national team’s training base during the November international window. According to ESPN, the 16-year-old Al Nassr academy forward has been named in Filipe Ramos’ 23-man squad for the 2027 European Under-17 Championship qualifying matches, having previously represented Portugal at U15 and U16 levels. The Portuguese footballing icon’s son, known popularly as “Cristianinho” (which translates to “Little Cristiano” in Portuguese), has previously represented the national side in the U-15 and U-16 levels since his debut in May 2025, making 13 appearances across both age group and scoring five goals. Portugal’s U17 team will play Andorra on November 11, Bulgaria on November 14 and Serbia on November 17, with all three matches scheduled to take place at the Portuguese Football Federation’s Cidade do Futebol training complex in Oeiras, near Lisbon. The team’s training camp is also scheduled to run at the facility from November 6 to 17. His father could also be at the same training base if he is included in Portugal’s senior squad for the upcoming international fixtures against Denmark on November 14 and Wales on November 17. However, Cristiano Ronaldo’s participation remains uncertain following reports that he was handed a 30-day suspension by the Portuguese Football Federation after leaving the national team camp during last month’s Nations League campaign. The 41-year-old remains Portugal’s all-time leading scorer in men’s international football, with 143 goals in 225 appearances. Ronaldo Jnr.’s maiden U17 call-up marks another step in his progression through Portugal’s youth national teams as he continues his development at Al Nassr’s academy. His father, meanwhile, is closing in on the 1,000-goal career milestone, having scored 985 goals. He recently netted a hat-trick for Al Nassr. In the past, Cristiano Ronaldo has spoken well about his son. At the Globe Soccer Awards in December 2020, he shared how his son’s diet and habits sometimes frustrated him, noting that the young boy liked drinking soda and eating crisps or fries even though he had great athletic potential. Ronaldo said: “We’ll see if he’ll be a great player. He’s not yet. Sometimes he drinks coke, he eats fries and he knows I get mad. I tell him to treadmill and then dive into cold water to recover, and he says: “Dad, but it’s so cold.” It’s normal because he’s young. He has potential. He is fast, he dribbles well, but that’s not enough. It takes a lot of hard work and dedication. I’m not going to pressure him to be a player. However, I especially want him to be the best, whether he’s a footballer or a doctor.” Vanguard News The post Ronaldo Jnr. earns first Portugal U17 call-up, could meet father at training ground appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ballot machine glitch hits New York county in US midterm election
item.description: Ballot machines malfunctioned Tuesday in a New York county that will help decide a closely contested House of Representatives race, though officials said votes for the US midterm elections are still being counted. Read Also: Trump cites immigration, Iran, tariffs in election day pitch The Westchester County Board of Elections “is aware of an issue involving paper ballots that is preventing voting machines from accepting ballots at polling locations throughout the county,” a statement read. It “wants to reassure every voter that your vote matters, your ballot will be secure and your vote will be counted,” with ballots instead placed in emergency bags. Parts of Westchester County are included in New York’s 17th district, where incumbent Republican Mike Lawler faces Democrat Cait Conley in a Hudson Valley seat won by Kamala Harris in the 2024 presidential election. The New York State Board of Elections said on X that there has been no disruption to voting. “Long-established emergency ballot procedures have been implemented, where completed ballots are secured, under bipartisan control, and will be counted,” it said. President Donald Trump and his allies have previously spread unproven conspiracy theories about voting machines, alleging that they are faulty or unreliable. item.title: High Court Hears Bid To Overturn Australia Social Media Ban
item.description: Australia’s landmark social media ban faces a legal test on Tuesday, as online platform Reddit urges the nation’s highest court to scrap the world-leading restrictions. Social media companies have been forced to purge millions of accounts after Australia banned under-16s from the likes of Facebook, TikTok and Reddit last December. The High Court of Australia will sit on Tuesday and Wednesday as Reddit, one of the most popular websites in the world, argues the laws are misguided and should be overturned. Reddit has highlighted a number of issues in its written submission to the court, pointing to problems enforcing the ban and a lack of scientific evidence about the harms of social media. “The evidence so far is that the effectiveness of the ban has been limited,” reads Reddit’s submission. Australia’s ban works by restricting children under 16 from holding accounts on the world’s biggest social media platforms. Map of Australia These platforms are responsible for weeding out underage users and face hefty fines if they are found to be falling short of their obligations. Reddit argued this approach was actually more dangerous, as registered accounts were governed by in-built safety features. Material posted on many online platforms and social media sites could still be accessed without an account, Reddit said. “Young people using other platforms without an account are also unable to be protected from exposure to particular harmful content as they previously had been,” its submission read. Australia said its restrictions would protect young users from graphic content, online predators and predatory algorithms designed to keep people scrolling. While there is a growing body of evidence about the harms of social media, Reddit argued there was no “scientific consensus”. Political discourse Reddit, which has also argued it should be exempt from the ban, said there was little research on whether certain platforms were safer than others. The High Court will also consider arguments from Australia’s Digital Freedom Project, which believes the ban restricts teens’ ability to take part in political discourse. “Social media is an important means of accessing news and engaging in political communication for young Australians, including children under 16,” the advocacy group argued in written submissions. “The restriction also risks removing beneficial sources of connection, support and participation,” it added.
